cards.name: ExportFilter
cards.summary: The pending-export object CorelDRAW returns from Document.ExportEx, Document.ExportBitmap and Bitmap.SaveAs: the file is not written until Finish is called, and in between the filter's own options dialog can be shown or reset. All its members live on the default interface ICorelExportFilter.
use_for: batch-export a logo selection to PNG at print resolution
export a page to SVG / AI / EPS from a pipeline and confirm the file was written
open the format's options dialog once while setting up an export preset by hand
avoid: saving the native .cdr: use Document.Save / SaveAs instead
one-shot exports with no need to touch the filter: Document.Export writes immediately and returns nothing
unattended runs with ShowDialog: it is modal and blocks the COM call
cards.how: Coclass whose default interface is ICorelExportFilter (members_on). A script never creates it directly; it gets one back from ActiveDocument.ExportEx(FileName, Filter, Range, Options), ActiveDocument.ExportBitmap(...) or Bitmap.SaveAs(...), then calls Finish to write the file.

key_members.name: Finish
key_members.use: performs the export and writes the file; without it nothing reaches disk

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: opens the filter's own options dialog (modal); returns False when the user cancels

key_members.name: HasDialog
key_members.use: True when this format has an options dialog worth showing

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: puts the filter's settings back to their defaults (unverified: exact scope)

key_members.name: ExternalSettings
key_members.use: hidden read-only string of the filter's settings, useful only for debugging

gotchas: Forgetting Finish is the classic bug: ExportEx / ExportBitmap return without error and no file appears.
Range cdrSelection with an empty selection fails or exports nothing (unverified: which).
Members sit on ICorelExportFilter, which the typelib flags hidden, so the VBA object browser does not list them; late binding and early binding both work.
ExportBitmap Width/Height 0 means the size follows from the resolution and the exported area (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim f As ExportFilter
Set f = ActiveDocument.ExportBitmap("C:\out\logo.png", cdrPNG, cdrSelection, cdrRGBColorImage, 0, 0, 300, 300)
f.Finish

cards.name: ExtrudeVanishingPoint
cards.summary: The vanishing point of an Extrude effect: the point the extruded sides run toward, whether it is locked to the object, locked to the page or shared with other extrusions, and its X/Y position. Moving it swings the direction of the fake-3D depth.
use_for: aim several extruded headline letters at one common vanishing point
nudge the perspective of an extruded logo from a script
lock the vanishing point to the page so moving the object changes its perspective
avoid: parallel extrusions (cdrExtrudeBackParallel / FrontParallel) have no real convergence: change the depth or direction instead
true 3D lighting / rotation: the extrude's other properties (shading, bevel) live on the Extrude effect object, not here
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGExtrudeVanishingPoint. Reached from an extrude effect: Shape.CreateExtrude(...) returns an Effect, and Effect.Extrude.VanishingPoint (IVGEffectExtrude.VanishingPoint) is this object; Shape.Effects.ExtrudeEffect finds an existing one.

key_members.name: PositionX
key_members.use: horizontal position of the vanishing point

key_members.name: PositionY
key_members.use: vertical position of the vanishing point

key_members.name: Share
key_members.use: makes this extrusion use the vanishing point of another extrude effect (Source)

key_members.name: Effects
key_members.use: the extrude effects that share this vanishing point

gotchas: Positions are in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit); whether they are page- or object-relative when locked to the shape is not confirmed (unverified).
After Share, Type reads cdrVPShared and moving one point moves all sharing extrusions (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim e As Effect
Set e = ActiveShape.CreateExtrude(cdrExtrudeSmallBack, cdrVPLockedToShape, 0, 0, 20)
With e.Extrude.VanishingPoint
  .Type = cdrVPLockedToPage
  .PositionX = 4: .PositionY = 8
End With

cards.name: Fill
cards.summary: The fill of a shape (or a free-standing fill made by Document.CreateFill): tells which fill type is active and applies uniform, fountain (gradient), pattern, texture, PostScript or hatch fills, or no fill. The sub-objects (Fountain, Pattern, Hatch ...) hold the type-specific settings.
use_for: paint generated shapes in exact CMYK brand colours
apply a gradient background to a poster panel
copy one object's fill onto many objects in a batch
preflight: find objects with no fill or with PostScript fills
avoid: outline colour: that is Shape.Outline, not Fill
partial text colouring: use TextRange.Fill on the character range instead of the text shape's Fill
unattended scripts with UserAssign: it opens a modal fill dialog
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFill. Reached as Shape.Fill, TextRange.Fill, TextFrame.Fill, TableCell.Fill, or created unattached with ActiveDocument.CreateFill / CreateUniformFill and then copied with CopyAssign.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: read-only cdrFillType: cdrNoFill, cdrUniformFill, cdrFountainFill, cdrPatternFill, cdrTextureFill, cdrPostscriptFill, cdrHatchFill

key_members.name: ApplyUniformFill
key_members.use: solid fill from a Color (CreateCMYKColor / CreateRGBColor ...)

key_members.name: UniformColor
key_members.use: get or set the solid colour of a uniform fill

key_members.name: ApplyFountainFill
key_members.use: gradient fill: start/end colour, type, angle, steps, midpoint, centre offset; returns the FountainFill

key_members.name: Fountain
key_members.use: the FountainFill settings of a fountain-filled shape

key_members.name: ApplyNoFill
key_members.use: removes the fill (shape becomes see-through inside)

key_members.name: ApplyPatternFill
key_members.use: two-colour, vector or bitmap pattern fill

key_members.name: ApplyTextureFill
key_members.use: texture fill by texture name and library

key_members.name: ApplyHatchFill
key_members.use: hatch fill from a hatch library by name or index

key_members.name: ApplyCustomHatchFill
key_members.use: hatch fill from angle and spacing; returns the HatchFill

key_members.name: Hatch
key_members.use: the HatchFill settings of a hatch-filled shape

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copies all properties of another Fill into this one

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: an unattached copy of this fill

key_members.name: CompareWith
key_members.use: True when two fills have the same properties

key_members.name: UserAssign
key_members.use: shows the fill dialog for the user (modal)

gotchas: Type is read-only: change the fill type with an Apply* method, never by assigning Type.
Reading Fountain / Pattern / Hatch on a shape whose Type is different does not give usable settings (error or empty object; unverified which).
CreateCMYKColor / CreateRGBColor take Long components; the usual 0-100 (CMYK) and 0-255 (RGB) ranges are not stated in the harvest (unverified).
UserAssign blocks the COM call until the dialog closes.
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(1, 1, 4, 3)
s.Fill.ApplyUniformFill CreateCMYKColor(0, 100, 100, 0)
If s.Fill.Type = cdrUniformFill Then s.Fill.UniformColor = CreateRGBColor(30, 30, 30)

review.changes: marked the CMYK 0-100 / RGB 0-255 range gotcha unverified (not in batch or harvest)

cards.name: FillMetadata
cards.summary: Descriptive metadata for a fill saved to or loaded from a fill file: multilingual Title, Description, Keywords, Subject, Copyright and Category, plus read-only creator tool, creation / modification dates and document IDs.
use_for: tag brand pattern fills with title, keywords and copyright when saving them for a shared library
read who made a fill file and when before reusing it
avoid: document-level metadata (title, keywords of the .cdr): that is the document's Metadata object, not this
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFillMetadata. Created with Application.CreateFillMetadata and passed as the optional Metadata argument of StyleFill.SaveFill(FileName, Metadata) or StyleFill.LoadFill(FileName, Metadata); StyleFill comes from Shape.Style.Fill.

key_members.name: Title
key_members.use: LocalizableString: set with DefaultLangString or SetLangString

key_members.name: Keywords
key_members.use: LocalizableString keywords used for search in content libraries

key_members.name: CreatorTool
key_members.use: read-only: application that created the fill file

key_members.name: ModificationDate
key_members.use: read-only last modification date and time

key_members.name: DocumentID
key_members.use: read-only ID shared by the fill and its derivatives

key_members.name: InstanceID
key_members.use: read-only ID of this fill file instance

key_members.name: DerivedFrom
key_members.use: read-only array of file IDs this fill is based on

gotchas: All properties are read-only references; the text ones are LocalizableString objects whose contents you change (DefaultLangString / SetLangString), not strings you assign.
The file format and extension SaveFill writes are not recorded in the harvest (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim md As FillMetadata
Set md = CreateFillMetadata
md.Title.DefaultLangString = "Brand stripes"
md.Keywords.DefaultLangString = "stripes, brand"
ActiveShape.Style.Fill.SaveFill "C:\fills\brand_stripes.fill", md

cards.name: FontList
cards.summary: Read-only list of the names of all fonts installed and available to CorelDRAW, as plain strings (base-1 index).
use_for: check that a brand font is installed before building a template
pick a fallback font in a batch job when the design font is missing
list installed fonts for a font-picker in a macro dialog
avoid: applying a font: set the text range's Font property instead
font styles and files: this is only names
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFontList, reached as Application.FontList (global FontList in VBA). Item is the default member, so FontList(i) works.

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the names

gotchas: Fonts installed while CorelDRAW is running may be missing until Application.ForceUpdateFontTable is called.
Names are family names as CorelDRAW shows them; weights / styles may not appear as separate entries (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim i As Long, found As Boolean
For i = 1 To FontList.Count
  If FontList.Item(i) = "Arial" Then found = True
Next i

cards.name: FountainColor
cards.summary: One colour stop of a fountain (gradient) fill or fountain transparency: its position along the gradient, colour, opacity, and the midpoint and blend type of the run to the next stop.
use_for: recolour the middle stop of a brand gradient
fade a gradient stop to transparent for a glow
shift a stop to tighten a highlight band on a metallic gradient
avoid: adding stops: use FountainColors.Add
changing the whole gradient type or angle: that is FountainFill
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFountainColor. Reached through a FountainFill's Colors collection: Fill.Fountain.Colors.Item(i), .First (start colour) or .Last (end colour).

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: get or set the stop colour

key_members.name: MidPoint
key_members.use: midpoint of the transition to the next stop

key_members.name: BlendType
key_members.use: cdrFountainFillBlendType: direct, rainbow clockwise / counter-clockwise, custom

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: removes the stop from the collection

gotchas: Position is read-only: use Move.
The start and end stops (First / Last) are fixed at the ends and cannot be moved or deleted (unverified).
Opacity is a byte; whether 0 means opaque or transparent is not confirmed (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim i As Long
With ActiveShape.Fill.Fountain.Colors
  For i = 2 To .Count - 1
    .Item(i).MidPoint = 30
  Next i
  .First.Color = CreateRGBColor(255, 200, 0)
End With

review.changes: dropped the invented 0-100 position range from summary; example now walks the inner stops by index instead of assuming Position 0 and 100

cards.name: FountainColors
cards.summary: The ordered collection of colour stops of a fountain fill or fountain transparency, with the start (First) and end (Last) stops and methods to add stops by colour or grey level.
use_for: build multi-stop gradients (sunset, chrome, rainbow) from a script
copy a gradient's stops into a palette report
set transparency ramps by grey level
avoid: two-colour gradients: ApplyFountainFill's StartColor / EndColor is enough
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFountainColors, reached as FountainFill.Colors (e.g. ActiveShape.Fill.Fountain.Colors). Item is the default member and is base 1.

key_members.name: AddGrayLevel
key_members.use: adds a stop by grey level (for fountain transparencies)

key_members.name: GrayLevel
key_members.use: grey level of the stop at Index

gotchas: Position is on the 0-100 scale of the gradient length (unverified for values outside it).
GrayLevel / AddGrayLevel are meant for transparency ramps where grey stands for transparency amount (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim ff As FountainFill
Set ff = ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(CreateRGBColor(255, 120, 0), CreateRGBColor(120, 0, 160), cdrLinearFountainFill, 90)
ff.Colors.Add CreateRGBColor(255, 255, 255), 50
Debug.Print ff.Colors.Count

cards.name: FountainFill
cards.summary: Settings of a fountain (gradient) fill or fountain transparency: linear, radial, conical or square type, the start / end handle positions, angle, colour stops, steps, centre offset, pad / reflect / repeat spread, scale, skew and smoothing.
use_for: gradient backgrounds and buttons
radial glow behind a product shot
repeat-reflect gradient stripes
fade-out transparency on a photo edge (via Transparency.Fountain)
avoid: mesh-like multi-directional colour: that is the Mesh Fill tool; the harvested object model has no mesh-fill object to script (only SelectionInformation.IsMeshFillPresent)
hard-edged bands only: a pattern or several shapes may be simpler
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGFountainFill. Returned by Fill.ApplyFountainFill(...), Fill.Fountain on a fountain-filled shape, and by Transparency.ApplyFountainTransparency / Transparency.Fountain for gradient transparency.

key_members.name: SetAngle
key_members.use: sets the gradient angle (Angle itself is read-only)

key_members.name: CenterOffsetX
key_members.use: centre offset in percent of object width

key_members.name: CenterOffsetY
key_members.use: centre offset in percent of object height

key_members.name: BlendAcceleration
key_members.use: how fast the blend runs between stops

key_members.name: IsTransparent
key_members.use: True when any stop has transparency

gotchas: Angle is read-only: call SetAngle.
EdgePad, BlendType, MidPoint and SetEdgePad are hidden legacy members; per-stop MidPoint / BlendType on FountainColor replace them.
The same object type describes a fountain transparency; there the stop colours act as transparency levels.
Steps 0 is the default passed by ApplyFountainFill and appears to mean automatic / smooth (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim ff As FountainFill
Set ff = ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(CreateCMYKColor(0, 60, 100, 0), CreateCMYKColor(0, 100, 100, 30), cdrRadialFountainFill)
ff.CenterOffsetX = -20: ff.CenterOffsetY = 20
ff.SpreadMethod = cdrFountainFillSpreadMethodPad
ff.Colors.Add CreateCMYKColor(0, 0, 0, 0), 40

review.changes: avoid no longer points scripts at a 'Mesh fill' object that does not exist in the harvest

cards.name: FrameWindow
cards.summary: One top-level CorelDRAW frame window (the main application window or an extra floating frame holding document views): caption, state, Windows handle, activation, tiling and the dock / view hosts it owns.
use_for: make sure the main window is restored before capturing screenshots of the app
get the window handle for targeted window messages from an automation harness
tile all document views for a side-by-side comparison
avoid: document windows / zoom: use the document's Window and ActiveView objects
closing documents: Close shuts every view in the frame and may raise save prompts
cards.how: Coclass with default interface ICUIFrameWindow, reached from the UI framework: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow, Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows.Item(i) or FrameWindows.Find(ID).

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: brings the frame to the front

key_members.name: IsActive
key_members.use: True when it is the active frame

key_members.name: IsMainFrame
key_members.use: True for the main application window

key_members.name: TileViews
key_members.use: tiles contained views horizontally or vertically

key_members.name: CombineViews
key_members.use: merges views into one view host

key_members.name: Close
key_members.use: closes the frame and all its views

gotchas: The typelib's description for this class reads 'ImageList class'; it is a copy-paste error, the members are those of a frame window.
A minimized frame gives blank screenshots: check State and call Restore first.
Close may raise modal save prompts that block an unattended run (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim fw As FrameWindow
Set fw = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow
If fw.State = cuiWindowStateMinimized Then fw.Restore
Debug.Print fw.Caption, fw.Handle

cards.name: FrameWindows
cards.summary: The collection of CorelDRAW's top-level frame windows (main window plus any extra floating frames), with lookup by index or ID and First / Last shortcuts.
use_for: find every CorelDRAW frame window before taking UI screenshots
locate a floating document frame by ID
avoid: listing open documents: use Application.Documents
cards.how: Coclass with default interface ICUIFrameWindows, reached as Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows. Item is the default member.
gotchas: Whether Item is base 0 or base 1 is not stated in the typelib (unverified); For Each avoids the question.
cards.example:
Dim w As FrameWindow
For Each w In Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows
  Debug.Print w.ID, w.Caption, w.IsMainFrame
Next w

cards.name: FrameWork
cards.summary: Root of CorelDRAW's UI framework: command bars, main menu and status bar, dockers, dialogs, message boxes, workspaces, frame windows, the background task manager, and the Automation object that runs any menu or toolbar command by GUID.
use_for: run a menu command that has no object-model call (Automation.InvokeItem with its GUID)
show or hide a docker from a macro
add a custom toolbar for in-house macros
import a team workspace
avoid: document work (shapes, pages, export): use Application / Document objects
ImportWorkspace on a shared machine: it changes the user's persistent workspace
cards.how: Coclass with default interface ICUIFrameWork, reached as Application.FrameWork (also from the UI framework's own ICUIApplication.FrameWork). The interface is flagged hidden but is the standard route to UI automation.

key_members.name: Automation
key_members.use: ICUIAutomation: InvokeItem(guid) runs a command, IsEnabled checks it

key_members.name: IsDockerVisible
key_members.use: True when the docker is visible

gotchas: Commands run through Automation.InvokeItem that open a dialog block the COM call until the dialog closes: wrap calls in a timeout.
ShowDialog and ShowMessageBox are modal.
Docker, dialog and command GUIDs are not in the type library; take them from the cdr_menu / cdr_tool cards or the workspace XML.
cards.example:
Dim cmd As String
cmd = "<command GUID from a cdr_menu card>"
With Application.FrameWork
  If .Automation.IsEnabled(cmd) Then .Automation.InvokeItem cmd
End With

cards.name: GlobalMacroStorage
cards.summary: The class behind each GMS project's ThisMacroStorage module: it has no callable members of its own and exists to receive application-wide events (document open / new / save / export / print / close, selection change, window activation, start and quit) through the DIVGApplicationEvents source interface.
use_for: auto-run a preflight before every export
stamp or log a document when it is saved
veto closing an unsaved job with QueryDocumentClose
initialise in-house tools when CorelDRAW starts
avoid: running a macro on demand from outside: use GMSManager.RunMacro
heavy work in SelectionChange: it fires on every click
cards.how: Coclass whose default interface _IGlobalMacroStorage (hidden) is empty and whose event source is DIVGApplicationEvents. In VBA you pick GlobalMacroStorage in the ThisMacroStorage module's object list and write handlers named GlobalMacroStorage_<Event>; event delivery follows Application.EventsEnabled.

key_members.name: DocumentOpen
key_members.use: event: Doc, FileName after a document opens

key_members.name: DocumentNew
key_members.use: event: a new document was created (FromTemplate, Template, IncludeGraphics)

key_members.name: QueryDocumentClose
key_members.use: event with Cancel: set True to stop the close

key_members.name: WindowActivate
key_members.use: event when a document window activates

gotchas: The event names above come from DIVGApplicationEvents (the source interface this class lists in implements); _IGlobalMacroStorage itself declares nothing.
Handlers fire only while the GMS project that holds them is loaded, and not while Application.EventsEnabled is False.
Query* events pass Cancel by reference; setting it True vetoes the action (unverified for every Query* event).
cards.example:
' ThisMacroStorage module of a GMS project
Private Sub GlobalMacroStorage_DocumentBeforeExport(ByVal Doc As Document, ByVal FileName As String, ByVal Filter As cdrFilter, ByVal SaveBitmap As Boolean)
  Debug.Print "exporting " & FileName
End Sub

review.changes: removed the invented 'only from a project loaded at start-up' claim

cards.name: GMSMacro
cards.summary: One macro (public Sub) inside a loaded GMS module: its name plus methods to run it, open it in the VBA editor or delete it.
use_for: list the tools a GMS module offers
run a parameterless macro found by name
avoid: macros that need arguments: use GMSManager.RunMacro with the arguments listed after the macro name
Delete on shared tool modules: it removes the Sub from the module
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGMSMacro, reached as GMSManager.Projects.Item(name).Macros.Item(name or index), or returned by GMSMacros.Create.

key_members.name: Edit
key_members.use: opens the VBA editor at the macro

gotchas: Run takes no parameters.
Edit opens the VBA editor window: never in unattended runs.
Delete changes the module source; it sticks once the module is saved.
cards.example:
Dim m As GMSMacro
For Each m In GMSManager.Projects.Item("MyTools").Macros
  Debug.Print m.Name
Next m
GMSManager.Projects.Item("MyTools").Macros.Item("ExportAll").Run

review.changes: avoid no longer tells the reader to pass RunMacro a parameter array

cards.name: GMSMacros
cards.summary: The collection of macros (public Subs) in one GMS module, with lookup by name or index and Create to add a new empty macro.
use_for: enumerate the macros of an in-house tool module
check a macro exists before calling GMSManager.RunMacro
avoid: running with arguments: GMSManager.RunMacro
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGMSMacros, reached as GMSProject.Macros (GMSManager.Projects.Item(name).Macros). Item is the default member.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of macros in the module

key_members.name: Create
key_members.use: creates a new macro with the given Name

gotchas: A locked or password-protected module may show no macros (unverified).
Create edits the module's VBA source (unverified: which code module receives it).
cards.example:
Dim ms As GMSMacros
Set ms = GMSManager.Projects.Item("MyTools").Macros
Debug.Print ms.Count
If ms.Count > 0 Then Debug.Print ms.Item(1).Name

cards.name: GMSManager
cards.summary: Entry point to Global Macro Storage: the folders where GMS modules live, the collection of loaded modules, and RunMacro, which runs any VBA macro by module and macro name with parameters, including from an outside COM client such as Python.
use_for: run an in-house VBA export or preflight macro from a Python pipeline
find the user and shared GMS folders to install a tool module
list which macro modules are loaded
avoid: menu commands that are not macros: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem
simple object-model work: call the COM objects directly instead of wrapping it in a macro
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGMSManager, reached as Application.GMSManager (VBA global GMSManager); from Python: app = win32com.client.Dispatch('CorelDRAW.Application.25'); app.GMSManager.

key_members.name: RunMacro
key_members.use: runs MacroName in module ModuleName; Parameters is a ParamArray, so the macro's arguments follow MacroName; returns the macro's result

gotchas: Parameters is a ParamArray (the typelib marks RunMacro vararg): list the arguments after MacroName and omit them when the macro takes none; wrapping them in Array() hands the macro one array argument.
MacroName is usually given as 'CodeModule.MacroName' (e.g. 'Module1.ExportAll') (unverified for every case).
A macro that shows a form or MsgBox blocks the COM call: keep pipeline macros UI-free.
cards.example:
Dim r As Variant
r = GMSManager.RunMacro("MyTools", "Module1.ExportAll", "C:\out", 300)
GMSManager.RunMacro "MyTools", "Module1.Preflight"
Debug.Print GMSManager.UserGMSPath

review.changes: RunMacro Parameters is vararg (typelib cParamsOpt -1), not a required array: fixed key_members use, the 'pass an empty array' gotcha and the Array(...) example

cards.name: GMSProject
cards.summary: One loaded GMS module (a .gms VBA project file): its name, file location, macros, modified / locked / password state, and Unload to drop it from memory.
use_for: check which file a tool module was loaded from
list a module's macros
unload a module before replacing its .gms file
avoid: editing code: use the VBA editor
loading new modules: GMSProjects.Load
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGMSProject, reached as GMSManager.Projects.Item(name or index), or returned by GMSProjects.Load / Create.

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: name as shown in the VBA editor

key_members.name: Locked
key_members.use: True when the project is unviewable

key_members.name: PasswordProtected
key_members.use: True when protected by a password

gotchas: Unload drops the module for this session; unsaved changes (Dirty) may be lost (unverified).
Renaming via Name may break toolbar buttons that call 'Module.Macro' by name (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim p As GMSProject
For Each p In GMSManager.Projects
  Debug.Print p.Name, p.FullFileName, p.Macros.Count
Next p

cards.name: GMSProjects
cards.summary: The collection of GMS modules CorelDRAW has loaded, with Load to bring in a .gms file (optionally copying it into the GMS folder, for the user or all users) and Create to make a new empty module.
use_for: install an in-house macro module from a pipeline
check a required tool module is loaded before RunMacro
avoid: running macros: GMSManager.RunMacro or GMSMacro.Run
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGMSProjects, reached as GMSManager.Projects. Item (default member) takes an index or the module name.

key_members.name: Load
key_members.use: loads a .gms file; CopyFile copies it into the GMS folder, ForAllUsers targets the shared folder

key_members.name: Create
key_members.use: creates a new empty GMS module

gotchas: Load with CopyFile / ForAllUsers writes into CorelDRAW's GMS folders: a persistent install, and ForAllUsers likely needs admin rights (unverified).
Item with a name that is not loaded raises an error: loop with For Each to test first (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim p As GMSProject
Set p = GMSManager.Projects.Load("C:\tools\PGDTools.gms", True)
Debug.Print p.Name, GMSManager.Projects.Count

cards.name: Grid
cards.summary: The document grid: visible or not, dot or line grid, snap-to-grid, and its horizontal / vertical spacing (or frequency).
use_for: switch on a layout grid and snapping for a modular poster
set a baseline-like spacing for icon design
hide the grid before screenshots
avoid: guidelines for specific positions: use Guide shapes
pixel grid for web export: that is a separate view option (unverified)
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGrid, reached as ActiveDocument.Grid.
gotchas: Spacing and frequency describe the same grid two ways (distance vs lines per unit); set one, not both (unverified).
Values are in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit) (unverified).
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.Grid
  .Type = cdrGridLine
  .SpacingX = 0.25: .SpacingY = 0.25
  .Visible = True: .Snap = True
End With

cards.name: Guide
cards.summary: Guideline-specific data of a guideline shape: horizontal, vertical or slanted type, its two defining points, slope angle, axis intercepts, and methods to move or rotate it by two points or by a point and angle.
use_for: place bleed / safe-area guides on every page of a print job
read existing guides to align generated objects
add slanted guides for a dynamic layout
avoid: regular grids: Grid
non-printing helper shapes that need styling: use ordinary shapes on a non-printing layer
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGGuide, reached as Shape.Guide on a shape whose Type is cdrGuidelineShape. Guides are created with Page.GuidesLayer.CreateGuide(x1, y1, x2, y2) or CreateGuideAngle(x, y, Angle) and listed with ActivePage.Guides(cdrHorizontalGuide / cdrVerticalGuide / cdrSlantedGuide).

key_members.name: SetPoints
key_members.use: moves / rotates the guide through two points

key_members.name: SetPointAndAngle
key_members.use: moves / rotates the guide through a point at a slope angle

key_members.name: GetPointAndAngle
key_members.use: returns a point and the slope angle

key_members.name: Preset
key_members.use: True for guides that come from a guide preset

key_members.name: InterceptX
key_members.use: X where the guide crosses the horizontal axis through the centre

key_members.name: InterceptY
key_members.use: Y where it crosses the vertical axis through the centre

key_members.name: CenterX
key_members.use: X of the guide point closest to the page centre

gotchas: Point and angle properties are read-only: move guides with SetPoints / SetPointAndAngle.
Preset guides may refuse edits until MakeEditable is called (unverified).
GetPoints / GetPointAndAngle return their values through [out] Double arguments (the typelib marks them out; the harvest does not record it): pass Double variables.
cards.example:
Dim g As Shape
Set g = ActivePage.GuidesLayer.CreateGuideAngle(0, 5.5, 0)
For Each g In ActivePage.Guides(cdrHorizontalGuide)
  Debug.Print g.Guide.Point1Y, g.Guide.Angle
Next g

review.changes: byref gotcha confirmed from the typelib ([out] params) instead of unverified; example now lists the horizontal guides it just created

cards.name: HatchFill
cards.summary: Settings of a hatch fill: one or more sets of parallel lines (HatchPatterns) with their own angle, spacing and line style, an optional background colour, scale, rotation and skew, and the library the hatch came from. Gives technical-drawing style cross-hatching inside a shape.
use_for: section hatching on architectural or engineering drawings
cross-hatched shading on a vintage illustration
map area patterns that survive black-only printing
avoid: bitmap or vector tile patterns: Pattern fill
smooth tone: Fountain fill or transparency
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchFill, returned by Fill.ApplyHatchFill(LibraryName, HatchNameOrIndex, ...), Fill.ApplyCustomHatchFill(Angle, Spacing, ...) and Fill.Hatch on a hatch-filled shape.

key_members.name: AddPattern
key_members.use: adds a line set: Angle, Spacing, Shift, origin, width, colour, style

key_members.name: BackColor
key_members.use: background colour; Nothing means no background

key_members.name: HasBackground
key_members.use: True when the background is opaque

key_members.name: Select
key_members.use: switches to a hatch from a library

key_members.name: ScaleLinesWithShape
key_members.use: line thickness scales with the shape

key_members.name: UseWorldCoordinates
key_members.use: align hatches of different objects in world coordinates

key_members.name: RotationAngle
key_members.use: extra rotation of the whole hatch

key_members.name: SkewAngle
key_members.use: extra skew of the whole hatch

key_members.name: AddToLibrary
key_members.use: stores this hatch in a library

gotchas: Spacing and line widths are in document units (unverified).
LibraryName arguments expect the library's Name (English), not the translated DisplayName (unverified).
AddToLibrary writes into a hatch library: a persistent change.
cards.example:
Dim h As HatchFill
Set h = ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyCustomHatchFill(45, 0.1)
h.AddPattern -45, 0.1
h.BackColor = CreateRGBColor(255, 250, 235)

cards.name: HatchFills
cards.summary: The hatch fills stored in one hatch library, found by name or index; each entry comes back as a Fill object carrying a hatch.
use_for: pick a library hatch by name for a drawing legend (take the names from the library first)
list a library's hatches for a style sheet
avoid: building hatches by numbers: Fill.ApplyCustomHatchFill
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchFills, reached as HatchLibrary.Fills (ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.Item(name).Fills). Item is the default member.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: hatch fill by name or index (returns a Fill)

key_members.name: Find
key_members.use: fill by name, Nothing when missing

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of fills in the library

gotchas: Entries are Fill objects, not HatchFill: copy them onto a shape with Shape.Fill.CopyAssign, read details via .Hatch.
Find returns Nothing rather than raising: test with Is Nothing.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary.Fills
  Debug.Print .Count
  If .Count > 0 Then ActiveShape.Fill.CopyAssign .Item(1)
End With

review.changes: removed invented hatch names (brick / insulation / concrete, Find("Brick")); example uses Item(1)

cards.name: HatchLibraries
cards.summary: All hatch fill libraries available to a document, with the default and the last-used (active) library and lookup by name or index.
use_for: find the library that holds a house hatch set
list available hatch libraries for a picker
avoid: applying a hatch directly: Fill.ApplyHatchFill takes the library name itself
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchLibraries, reached as ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries. Item is the default member.

key_members.name: Find
key_members.use: library by name, Nothing when missing

gotchas: Find takes the library name; the translated DisplayName may differ in localised installs (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim lib As HatchLibrary
For Each lib In ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries
  Debug.Print lib.Name, lib.DisplayName, lib.Fills.Count
Next lib

cards.name: HatchLibrary
cards.summary: One hatch fill library: its English and translated names, its fills, whether it is the active library, and Activate to make it current in the UI.
use_for: switch the hatch picker to a project library
read a library's fills for a legend
avoid: adding new hatches: HatchFill.AddToLibrary
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchLibrary, reached from HatchLibraries.Item / Find / DefaultLibrary / ActiveLibrary, or HatchFill.Library.

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: translated name shown in the UI

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: makes the library active in the UI

gotchas: The harvested description of Fills says it returns a number; it returns the HatchFills collection (type IVGHatchFills).
cards.example:
Dim lib As HatchLibrary
Set lib = ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary
lib.Activate
Debug.Print lib.Name, lib.Fills.Count

cards.name: HatchPattern
cards.summary: One set of parallel lines inside a hatch fill: angle, spacing, origin, per-line shift (for dashed offsets) and the outline (width, colour, dash style) the lines are drawn with.
use_for: tune line angle and spacing of a section hatch
make the second line set of a cross-hatch thinner or coloured
avoid: changing the whole hatch's scale or rotation: HatchFill.SetFillScale / RotationAngle
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchPattern, reached as HatchFill.Patterns.Item(i) or returned by HatchFill.AddPattern.

key_members.name: Shift
key_members.use: extra horizontal shift of successive lines

key_members.name: ShiftPercent
key_members.use: shift as a percentage of the dash pattern

key_members.name: SetProperties
key_members.use: sets the common properties in one call

gotchas: Outline is read-only as a reference; change its properties (Width, Color) rather than assigning a new outline.
Units follow the document unit (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim p As HatchPattern
Set p = ActiveShape.Fill.Hatch.Patterns.Item(1)
p.Angle = 30: p.Spacing = 0.15
p.Outline.Width = 0.01

cards.name: HatchPatterns
cards.summary: The line sets that make up one hatch fill, by index, with Reset to cut the hatch back to a single default line set.
use_for: walk all line sets of a hatch to restyle them
reset a complex library hatch to a simple single-line hatch
avoid: adding line sets: HatchFill.AddPattern
cards.how: Coclass with default interface IVGHatchPatterns, reached as HatchFill.Patterns.

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: deletes all but one line set and resets it

gotchas: Reset is destructive for the current hatch: it removes every line set but one.
cards.example:
Dim p As HatchPattern
For Each p In ActiveShape.Fill.Hatch.Patterns
  p.Outline.Color = CreateCMYKColor(0, 0, 0, 100)
Next p

cards.name: IColorConversionHandler
cards.summary: Call-back interface meant to be handed to StructColorConversionOptions.ColorConversionHandler to decide what happens when colour profiles are missing or mismatched on open / import. In the 25.1 type library it declares no members, so a script has nothing to implement or call.
use_for: recognising the type when reading ColorConversionHandler; nothing to script with it
avoid: handling profile mismatches: set the colour policy and source / target profile lists on StructColorConversionOptions (ColorPolicy, SourceColorProfileList, TargetColorProfileList) instead
cards.how: Dispinterface inheriting IDispatch with an empty member list. It is the type of IVGStructColorConversionOptions.ColorConversionHandler, which the harvest describes as a custom call-back used when missing or mismatched profiles are encountered.

key_members.name: IColorConversionHandler
key_members.use: the interface itself: the harvest lists no members on it

gotchas: Zero members in the type library: implementing it from VBA or Python gives the host nothing to call (what the host expects is undocumented in the harvest; unverified).
cards.example:
Dim opt As Object
Set opt = CreateStructImportOptions
Debug.Print opt.ColorConversionOptions.ColorConversionHandler Is Nothing

cards.name: ICorelExportFilter
cards.summary: Default interface of ExportFilter, also implemented by every per-format export filter library (AI, BMP, CGM, EPS, GIF, JPG, JP2, PNG, SVG, TGA, WEBP, WMF ...): Reset, ShowDialog / HasDialog for the format's options, and Finish to actually write the file.
use_for: finish an export started with ExportEx / ExportBitmap
show a format's export dialog once while setting up a job
avoid: unattended jobs with ShowDialog (modal)
plain exports where Document.Export is enough
cards.how: Hidden dual interface; you hold it whenever ExportEx, ExportBitmap or Bitmap.SaveAs returns. Dim the variable As ExportFilter (the coclass) or As Object.

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: shows the filter's options dialog (hWnd optional); False on cancel

key_members.name: HasDialog
key_members.use: True when the filter has an options dialog

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: restores the filter's default settings (unverified: scope)

gotchas: Hidden in the object browser, so autocomplete does not offer Finish; it still works.
Per-format options are reached through the filter-specific type libraries listed in also_in (unverified: which properties each adds).
cards.example:
Dim f As ExportFilter
Set f = ActiveDocument.ExportEx("C:\out\icon.svg", cdrSVG, cdrSelection)
If f.HasDialog Then Debug.Print "has options dialog"
f.Finish

cards.name: ICorelImportFilter
cards.summary: The pending-import object returned by Layer.ImportEx: lets the format's import dialog be shown or reset, and places the file on the layer when Finish is called. Also implemented by the per-format import filter libraries (CGM, DSF, DXF, HPGL, SVG ...).
use_for: import an SVG / DXF / AI file onto a chosen layer from a pipeline
show an import options dialog once while setting up
avoid: simple imports: Layer.Import does it in one call
opening a file as its own document: use OpenDocument
cards.how: Hidden dual interface returned by ActiveLayer.ImportEx(FileName, Filter, Options); Options comes from CreateStructImportOptions.

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: shows the import options dialog (modal); False on cancel

key_members.name: HasDialog
key_members.use: True when the filter has an options dialog

gotchas: Nothing is placed until Finish.
Imported objects usually end up selected, so ActiveSelection picks them up (unverified).
Hidden interface: not listed in the object browser.
cards.example:
Dim f As Object
Set f = ActiveLayer.ImportEx("C:\in\art.svg", cdrSVG)
f.Finish
Debug.Print ActiveSelectionRange.Count

cards.name: ICorelScriptTools
cards.summary: Legacy CorelSCRIPT helper library kept for old macros: unit conversion (inches, points, picas, ciceros, didots, centimetres, angles), file and folder utilities, file / folder / colour / font picker dialogs, registry reads, date helpers and the wait cursor.
use_for: convert points or picas to another unit in an old-style macro
make an output folder or find files without the VBA FileSystemObject
show a wait cursor during a long batch
avoid: new code: VBA / Python file APIs and Application.ConvertUnits-style document units are clearer
unattended runs with GetFileBox / GetFolder / GetColor / GetFont: they open modal dialogs
Kill / RmFolder unless the path is certain: they delete permanently
cards.how: Dual interface reached as Application.CorelScriptTools (VBA: CorelScriptTools). All members are plain methods.

key_members.name: LengthConvert
key_members.use: converts a length between unit codes (FromUnit, ToUnit, Value)

key_members.name: AngleConvert
key_members.use: converts an angle between unit codes

gotchas: In CorelSCRIPT the To*/From* functions convert to / from tenths of a micron, its internal unit (unverified in 25.1).
LengthConvert / AngleConvert take numeric unit codes whose meaning is not in the harvest (unverified; not necessarily cdrUnit).
GetFileBox, GetFolder, GetColor and GetFont are modal dialogs.
cards.example:
Dim t As Object, outDir As String
Set t = Application.CorelScriptTools
outDir = t.GetTempFolder() & "pgd_out"
t.MkFolder outDir
t.BeginWaitCursor
' ... long batch ...
t.EndWaitCursor

cards.name: ICUIApplication
cards.summary: The UI framework's application object, mainly for add-ons that build their own dockers and dialogs: the top-level data context and data-source registration for UI binding, image lists, bitmaps, status text, screen rectangles and localized strings.
use_for: load an icon file as a bitmap for a custom docker or message box
register a data source for a custom XAML / .NET docker
fetch a localized UI string by GUID
avoid: document and shape work: IVGApplication (CorelDRAW.Application)
cards.how: Dual interface reached as Application.FrameWork.Application (ICUIFrameWork.Application) or a data source proxy's Application.

key_members.name: RegisterDataSource
key_members.use: registers a data-source factory under a name

key_members.name: CreateDataSourceFactory
key_members.use: wraps a dispatch object as a data-source factory

key_members.name: CreateBitmapImage
key_members.use: bitmap from a file name, byte array or stream

gotchas: Data-source registration is for add-ons whose UI binds to it; from plain VBA it has little effect (unverified).
Registered data sources may persist for the session; unregister them when the add-on unloads (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim ui As Object, img As Object
Set ui = Application.FrameWork.Application
Set img = ui.CreateBitmapImage("C:\icons\pgd.png")
Debug.Print img.Valid, img.Width, img.Height

cards.name: ICUIAutomation
cards.summary: CorelDRAW's internal UI-automation interface (described in the typelib as 'Internal Automation - Do not use'): walk command bars by GUID, read captions, enabled state and screen positions of items, show bars, and invoke any command or dialog button by GUID. It is the route PGD uses for cdr_guid commands.
use_for: run a menu command that has no object-model method (InvokeItem with the command GUID)
check a command is enabled before invoking it
map a toolbar or menu's items to GUIDs and captions
press a button inside an open dialog by GUID (InvokeDialogItem)
avoid: anything the object model can do directly: those calls are faster and do not depend on UI state
commands that open modal dialogs in unattended runs
cards.how: Hidden dual interface reached as Application.FrameWork.Automation.

key_members.name: InvokeItem
key_members.use: runs the command with this GUID

key_members.name: IsEnabled
key_members.use: True when the command can run now

key_members.name: InvokeDialogItem
key_members.use: presses an item in a dialog (GuidDialog, GuidItem)

key_members.name: GetNumItemsOnBar
key_members.use: number of items on a bar

key_members.name: GetItem
key_members.use: GUID of the item at Index on a bar; HasSubBar tells if it opens a sub-bar

key_members.name: GetSubBar
key_members.use: writes the sub-bar GUID of GuidBar into the [out] GuidSubBar argument; returns True when there is one

key_members.name: ShowBar
key_members.use: shows / hides a bar by GUID

key_members.name: GetItemInstanceHwnd
key_members.use: window handle of an item instance

key_members.name: GetControlDataEx
key_members.use: same, scoped to a parent GUID

key_members.name: GetActiveMenuItemGuid
key_members.use: GUID of an item in the open menu

key_members.name: GetActiveMenuItemScreenRect
key_members.use: screen rectangle of an item in the open menu

gotchas: Flagged hidden and 'do not use': members may change between versions without notice.
InvokeItem on a command that opens a dialog blocks until the dialog closes: give the call a timeout and treat a hang as a modal dialog.
A disabled command (IsEnabled False) does nothing when invoked (unverified: silently or with an error).
Invoke (no 'Item') is hidden; use InvokeItem.
cards.example:
Dim a As Object, g As String
Set a = Application.FrameWork.Automation
g = "<command GUID from a cdr_menu card>"
If a.IsEnabled(g) Then a.InvokeItem g
Debug.Print a.GetCaptionText(g)

review.changes: GetSubBar use corrected: it returns a Boolean and hands the GUID back through an out argument

cards.name: ICUIBackgroundTask
cards.summary: Interface an add-on implements to run work off the UI thread through the framework's task manager: RunTask does the work, FinalizeTask runs afterwards (usually on the UI thread), QuitTask handles cancellation and FreeTask cleans up; Name is shown in the UI.
use_for: long analysis (font scan, file indexing) in a custom add-on without freezing CorelDRAW
avoid: touching documents or shapes inside RunTask: do that in FinalizeTask on the UI thread
simple macros: a normal VBA loop with a wait cursor is enough
cards.how: Dual interface inheriting ICUITask. You implement it and pass the object to Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunInBackground(priority, task) with a cuiTaskPriority (kMaybeLater, kLater, kSoon, kASAP); the framework calls the members, you never call them yourself.

key_members.name: RunTask
key_members.use: the work; called by the framework, possibly on a background thread

key_members.name: FinalizeTask
key_members.use: called after RunTask unless removed, usually on the UI thread

key_members.name: QuitTask
key_members.use: called when the task is asked to quit; may come from another thread

key_members.name: FreeTask
key_members.use: called before the task is disposed

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: name shown for the task in the UI

gotchas: Every member description says 'Do not call this yourself'.
Whether a VBA class module can implement this derived interface is not confirmed; it is aimed at .NET / C++ add-ons (unverified).
QuitTask may arrive on a different thread than RunTask: guard shared state.
cards.example:
' caller side; task is an object implementing ICUIBackgroundTask
Dim tm As Object
Set tm = Application.FrameWork.TaskManager
tm.RunInBackground kSoon, task

cards.name: ICUIBitmapImage
cards.summary: A bitmap held by the UI framework (made from a file, byte array or stream) for icons and message-box images; exposes only whether it loaded and its pixel size.
use_for: check a custom toolbar or docker icon loaded before using it
pass an image to FrameWork.ShowMessageBox
avoid: bitmaps in the drawing: those are Shape / Bitmap objects of the document
cards.how: Dual interface returned by ICUIApplication.CreateBitmapImage(ImageData, MaxSize), reached via Application.FrameWork.Application.
gotchas: A wrong path gives an object with Valid False rather than an error (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim img As Object
Set img = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateBitmapImage("C:\icons\pgd.png")
If img.Valid Then Debug.Print img.Width & " x " & img.Height

cards.name: ICUICommandBar
cards.summary: One command bar: a toolbar, the main menu, a popup menu, the status bar or the property bar. Read its type, name and controls, show / hide or enable it, protect it from user changes, pop it up, reset or delete it.
use_for: add an in-house toolbar for pipeline macros
hide toolbars before taking clean UI screenshots
pop up a custom context menu from a macro
avoid: running a single command: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem
permanent UI edits on a shared workstation: they persist in the workspace
cards.how: Dual interface reached as Application.CommandBars.Item(name or index) (Item is default, so CommandBars(1) or CommandBars("<bar name>")), Application.MainMenu, Application.StatusBar, or returned by CommandBars.Add.

key_members.name: ShowPopup
key_members.use: shows the bar as a popup at x, y

gotchas: Customisations persist in the user's workspace unless the bar / controls were added with Temporary True.
Left, Top, Width, Height and Position are hidden members; use SetWidth / Visible rather than relying on them.
Use Name, not NameLocal, so scripts work in every UI language.
cards.example:
Dim bar As Object
Set bar = Application.CommandBars.Add("PGD Tools", cuiBarFloating, True)
bar.Controls.AddCustomButton "<macro category GUID>", "PGDTools.Module1.ExportAll"
bar.Visible = True

review.changes: replaced the invented 'Standard' bar name in how

cards.name: ICUICommandBarMode
cards.summary: One mode of a command bar: a named set of controls the bar shows in a given context, as the property bar does for each tool or selection type.
use_for: inspect which controls the property bar shows for a tool
add a macro button to one property-bar context
avoid: ordinary toolbars: they normally have a single control set on ICUICommandBar.Controls
cards.how: Dual interface reached as CommandBar.Modes.Item(name or index).
gotchas: Mode names are internal and undocumented; list them first (unverified naming).
Which bars besides the property bar have several modes is not confirmed (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim m As Object
For Each m In Application.CommandBars.Item(1).Modes
  Debug.Print m.Name, m.Controls.Count
Next m

cards.name: ICUICommandBarModes
cards.summary: The collection of modes (context-specific control sets) of one command bar, by index or name.
use_for: enumerate the property bar's tool contexts
avoid: changing controls: go to a mode's Controls
cards.how: Dual interface reached as CommandBar.Modes. Item (default member) takes an index or a name.
gotchas: Index base is not stated (unverified); For Each avoids it.
cards.example:
Dim ms As Object
Set ms = Application.CommandBars.Item(1).Modes
Debug.Print ms.Count

cards.name: ICUICommandBars
cards.summary: All command bars of CorelDRAW (toolbars, menus, status and property bars), with lookup by name or index and Add to create a new, optionally temporary, toolbar.
use_for: create a temporary toolbar for a session's macros
list toolbars to hide them for screenshots
avoid: menu commands: FrameWork.Automation
cards.how: Dual interface reached as Application.CommandBars or Application.FrameWork.CommandBars. Item is the default member.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: new bar: Name, Position (cuiBarPosition, default cuiBarFloating), Temporary

gotchas: Add without Temporary True creates a bar that persists in the workspace.
Adding a bar whose name already exists fails (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim b As Object
For Each b In Application.CommandBars
  Debug.Print b.Name, b.Visible, b.BuiltIn
Next b
Application.CommandBars.Add "PGD Temp", cuiBarTop, True

cards.name: ICUIControl
cards.summary: One control (button, menu item, custom control) on a command bar: its caption, tooltip, description, size, visibility, command ID (GUID) and custom icon, plus free Tag / Parameter slots for macro data.
use_for: read the GUID behind a toolbar button to invoke it later
label and icon a custom macro button
hide a control for a simplified kiosk workspace
avoid: running the control's command from code: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem with its ID
cards.how: Dual interface reached as CommandBar.Controls.Item(i), or returned by Controls.Add / AddCustomButton / AddCustomControl / AddToggleButton.

key_members.name: ID
key_members.use: read-only GUID of the control's command

gotchas: SetIcon is hidden; use SetCustomIcon or SetIcon2.
Changes persist in the workspace unless the control was added as Temporary.
cards.example:
Dim c As Object
For Each c In Application.CommandBars.Item(1).Controls
  Debug.Print c.ID, c.Caption
Next c

review.changes: example uses CommandBars.Item(1) instead of the invented 'Standard' bar name

cards.name: ICUIControlData
cards.summary: Read access to the data behind a UI control, returned by FrameWork.Automation.GetControlData(guid): GetValue reads one named property of that control. Which property names exist is not in the type library.
use_for: reading a control's current state (for example a toggle or value) during UI automation, once the property names are known
avoid: state the object model exposes directly (document, shape, tool settings): read it there
cards.how: Hidden dual interface returned by ICUIAutomation.GetControlData(Guid) or GetControlDataEx(GuidParent, Guid).

key_members.name: GetValue
key_members.use: value of the property named PropertyName

gotchas: Property names are undocumented; guesses fail at run time (unverified which names work).
Part of the internal automation surface: may change between versions.
cards.example:
Dim d As Object
Set d = Application.FrameWork.Automation.GetControlData("<control GUID>")
Debug.Print d.GetValue("<property name>")

cards.name: ICUIControls
cards.summary: The controls on a command bar or command bar mode, with methods to add a built-in command by ID, a macro button, a custom .NET control or a toggle button for a docker, and to remove controls.
use_for: put an in-house macro on a toolbar
add a toggle button that opens a custom docker
remove clutter controls from a custom bar
avoid: permanent edits of built-in bars on shared machines: pass Temporary True
cards.how: Dual interface reached as CommandBar.Controls or CommandBarMode.Controls. Item takes a long index.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: adds a built-in control by ControlID (GUID), at Index, Temporary

key_members.name: AddCustomButton
key_members.use: adds a button that runs Command (a macro) in CategoryID

key_members.name: AddCustomControl
key_members.use: adds a custom control by class name from a .NET assembly

key_members.name: AddToggleButton
key_members.use: adds a button that shows / hides the UI element with this GUID

gotchas: Index 0 in the Add methods appears to mean 'append at the end' (unverified).
AddCustomButton needs the category GUID of the macro command category; it is not in the harvest (unverified value).
Without Temporary True the change is saved into the workspace.
cards.example:
Dim bar As Object, c As Object
Set bar = Application.CommandBars.Add("PGD Temp", cuiBarFloating, True)
Set c = bar.Controls.AddCustomButton("<macro category GUID>", "PGDTools.Module1.ExportAll", 0, True)
c.Caption = "Export all"
c.ToolTipText = "Run the PGD export macro"
bar.Visible = True

review.changes: example adds the button to a temporary bar instead of the invented 'Standard' bar
